en: I bow to that Gopāla, who exists for all time, from whom this manifold and inconceivable universe was born; in whom, the self of bliss, it eternally delights; and into whom this entire world finally goes to its dissolution. || 1 ||

I bow to that Gopāla, the eternal Time, through whose ignorance the multitude of birth, old age, and disease arises, and upon knowing whom all that quickly perishes here; and having gone to whom, one never returns again to the ground of worldly existence.

I bow to that Gopāla, who, remaining within as the inner controller, incessantly restrains everything; whom no person knows, though he dwells within the self; and under whose control this entire universe stands at all times. 3.

I bow to that Gopāla, the eternal Time, who at a time when Dharma suffers humiliation here through unrighteousness and by those of evil conduct with faces like fish, protects the circle of the earth in various forms.

I perpetually worship that Gopāla, who is the form of light, into whom the practitioners of yoga— having suppressed all defects of the senses through breath-control (prāṇāyāma) and having restrained the mind in samādhi within the heart— are immersed in bliss.
I perpetually worship that Gopāla, in whom the sun, the moon, the hosts of stars, the sacrificial fire, and even lightning never shine; yet by whose radiance this entire world shines forth.

I bow to that Gopāla, whose feet are worshipped by Brahmā, Indra, Āditya, and Śiva; whom the Vedas have declared to be true knowledge and bliss; he who, as the infinite Ananta, reclines upon his infinite body in the ocean of milk throughout all time.
Those who follow Śiva call him Śiva; others, Gaṇanātha; some, Śakti; and likewise others, the Sun—due to differences in their understanding.
I bow to that Gopāla, the single possessor of all powers, who shines in manifold forms throughout all time.

That man of steady mind who indeed studies this *Śrīmad-Gopālāṣṭaka* daily with devotion quickly casts off the entire mass of his sins and attains the meritorious abode of Viṣṇu, from which there is no falling back. (9)
Thus ends the Śrī Gopālāṣṭaka composed by the venerable Paramahaṃsa Svāmī Brahmānanda.
